complexity_ledger.narrative: MF-033 gives the effect oracle a SECOND observer that reaches across the process boundary the in-process EffectSandbox cannot cross. MF-028 measured that every adapter in this repository shells out, so the sandbox saw only the spawn and the verdict was `unobservable` forever. scripts/effect_conformance.py now carries WorkingTreeObserver: a working-tree snapshot diff (pure stdlib, no privileges, no dependency, runtime-agnostic) that snapshots roots before an execution window and diffs them after, turning a child's created/changed files into filesystem.write and vanished files into filesystem.delete. diff_effects grew an `out_of_process=` parameter carrying OutOfProcessObservation records -- POSITIVE evidence of which effect axes an observer covered -- and narrows a spawn's process-boundary finding to name only the axes still unwatched. MEASURED on this repo's own surface (results/observe_out_of_process.py drives the real, shelling-out ScaffoldProjectAdapter through its real subprocess.run against the real five declared ports): BEFORE = 2 observed effects, spec_tree DEAD, blanket boundary, verdict unobservable (the MF-028 state). AFTER = 17 observed effects, 15 child writes recovered out-of-process (all matching **/specs/**), spec_tree EXERCISED, a real GAP surfaced (ScaffoldProject's undeclared python spawn), and the boundary finding narrowed to "filesystem observed; network.connect, network.http, process.spawn unobserved". Verdict STILL unobservable -- honestly, because a filesystem diff cannot see a child's network, and that residual is named precisely (acceptance criterion branch 2). The four other ports read as honest dead_surface from a reduced single-action demo; declarations preserved, not deleted. MF-027 POLARITY SURVIVED, proven by tests (TestPolaritySurvivesOutOfProcessObservation): a spawn with no out-of-process evidence is still fully unobservable; filesystem-only coverage still leaves the network unobservable; only positive coverage of EVERY axis discharges a boundary (which a filesystem-only observer never reaches); a runtime refusal is untouched; and `out_of_process` is an evidence parameter, never a suppression flag (empty evidence downgrades nothing). report.ok still consults only the finding lists. COST PROBE (results/cost-report.md, the owner-decision deliverable): the OBSERVATION mechanism generalizes fully and cheaply to the filesystem axis of all four other oracle actions (they all write into **/results/** or **/specs/** via a child). But that does NOT make them case-executable: their signal is a VERDICT, not a filesystem tree, and comparing a verdict is per-oracle projection work with no shared shape (MF-028 banded them HARD/BLOCKED for exactly this). Recommendation: RUN THE ORACLES ADVISORILY rather than chasing per-oracle verdict projection -- reaching a `clean` effect verdict on a shelling-out repo needs either network syscall capture (privileged, non-portable) or in-process invocation of every adapter (MF-028's "large" axis), and the payoff (a blocking gate) is what the 2026-07-20 advisory reframe already retired. Zero TLA+ delta; validation matrix green (TLC 231,621/depth 25, spec-unit 60 over 2 targets, 526 repo units, specWorkflow 8/8 + cliWorkflow 2/2).

ticket.objective: MF-028 moved observed effects 0 -> 6 and the verdict still refuses as unobservable, because every adapter shells out and the sandbox sees only in-process CPython. run() ALONE DOES NOT RESTORE ORACLE 3 -- this is a second axis of work that was absent from the plan. Either route adapter work in-process so the existing sandbox sees it, or add out-of-process observation (subprocess wrapper, syscall capture, or container-level recorder) behind the same port-declaration schema. MF-027 established the polarity that must be preserved: observability is granted only on positive evidence and anything unrecognised REFUSES rather than passing.
